title: Ward Systems Walk
brief: You walk a day-surgery ward at Meridian Care as an internal auditor, a week before the certification audit. This visit covers management system topics only. Clinical decisions, clinical standards, and law are outside its scope; the investigator does not judge clinical care. Look at documents, equipment status, records, competence, and information handling across the ward. You have 12 visit points.

actions.label: Protocol sheets in the ward folder
General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: The ward folder holds admission protocol sheet version 3; the document system shows version 4 approved 6 weeks ago.
evidence.whyItMatters: Current approved documents must be available where work is done.
evidence.missedExplanation: Compare version numbers with the document system.

evidence.text: 2 workstations at the nurses station show patient records unattended and unlocked for 10 minutes (workstations WS-2 and WS-4).
evidence.whyItMatters: Personal information belongs to the patient and must be protected.
evidence.missedExplanation: Observe screens as well as paper.

evidence.text: A blood pressure monitor (asset BP-17) in use carries a verification label overdue by 5 weeks.
evidence.whyItMatters: Measuring devices must be verified at the planned interval. The device owner decides on any clinical review of readings.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read verification labels on devices in use.

evidence.text: Handover sheets for 3 of 14 cases yesterday have blank sections for pending results (form HS-2 section C).
evidence.whyItMatters: Controlled service delivery includes complete handover records.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read every section of handover forms.

evidence.text: Competence records for 6 agency staff on shift are current and checked by the ward.
evidence.whyItMatters: Competence is verified for temporary staff.

evidence.text: Patient feedback summary for quarter 2 is collected but no actions are recorded against 3 recurring comments about discharge information.
evidence.whyItMatters: Feedback should be analyzed and used.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask what was done with feedback.

evidence.text: Supplies received this week have certificates checked and filed.
Ward manager: "Revised forms are emailed; not everyone reads email on shift." 2 staff were unaware of version 4.
evidence.whyItMatters: Communication of changes could be improved.

evidence.text: Equipment service log is up to date for 31 devices.
Some shelf labels are handwritten but legible and current.
The staff photo board is out of date by 2 names.

decisions.prompt: What should the ward manager address today?
options: Remove device BP-17 from use pending the owner's review, lock unattended screens, and replace protocol version 3 with version 4
decisions.rationale: Issues affecting information protection, device status, and document use come first. Any clinical follow-up is for the responsible clinicians.

containment: Withdraw BP-17 and refer the question of earlier readings to the device owner and responsible clinicians
correction: Replace protocol version 3, complete handover sections, and record actions on feedback
cause: Document changes and device due dates rely on email and memory, and screens do not lock automatically
corrective: Brief revised forms at shift handover, add device due alerts, and enable automatic screen lock
effectiveness: Repeat the walk monthly for three months

debriefText.found: You covered documents, devices, records, information, and feedback.
debriefText.missed: Unattended screens are easy to walk past.
debriefText.falseFinding: Legible handwritten labels and a photo board are not findings.
